summary: Defines a DHCP option that lets a client ask for an address on a particular subnet. This helps when a relay agent or server serves several subnets and the client wants to say which one it needs. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: When you ask for a seat at a big hall with many sections, you can say which section you want. This lets a computer ask for a particular part of the network.

questions: how to request an address from a specific subnet
what is the dhcp subnet selection option
how does a dhcp server choose a subnet
why is the dhcp subnet selection option disabled by default
subtitle: A DHCP option that lets a client name the subnet it wants its address to come from.

tldr.problem: A DHCP server normally picks the subnet from where the request came in. A device that requests addresses on behalf of clients on other networks cannot get addresses on those networks that way.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3011 defines the subnet selection option, DHCP option code 118, which carries one IPv4 subnet address. When the server is set up to honor it, the option overrides the server's usual way of choosing a subnet.
tldr.outcome: A client can ask for an address on a particular subnet. Because this lets a client reach address pools beyond its own subnet, servers must ship with the feature switched off.

today: RFC 3011 is a Proposed Standard published in November 2000, and it has not been obsoleted or updated by another RFC.

sections.title: How a DHCP Server Picks a Subnet
sections.content:
The Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (RFC 2131) hands out configuration to hosts on a TCP/IP network, and RFC 2132 defines the options that DHCP packets can carry. RFC 3011 adds one more option.

Normally the server works out which subnet the request came from, then allocates an address on that subnet or on a subnet on the same network segment. It finds the originating subnet in one of two ways: from the subnet address of the giaddr field in the DHCP packet header, or, if giaddr is zero, from the subnet address of the local interface that received the packet.

The new subnet selection option lets the client state the subnet itself, and it takes precedence over both of those methods. The RFC uses the key words MUST and SHOULD as defined in RFC 2119.
sections.eli5: Usually the helper decides which section of the hall you sit in, based on the door you came through. This option lets you say which section you want instead.

sections.title: The Motivating Example
sections.content:
The RFC's example is a device, such as a RAS device, that allocates addresses on behalf of its own clients. It gets the addresses through DHCP and then manages them among those clients.

The device sits on a private internal network, where the DHCP server lives. It is also connected to one or more external networks, which is where its clients are. The internal network is not IP connected to the external ones, although inside the device there is connectivity between them, for example through the backplane.

That is the problem. The DHCP requests cannot come from the external networks, because packets cannot be routed between them and the internal network. So they must come from the internal network, and the server would then allocate addresses on the internal subnet, which is not what is wanted. The device sends its request on the internal subnet but includes the subnet selection option with the address of the external subnet it needs. The server then allocates on the requested subnet instead.
sections.eli5: Imagine a receptionist who can only phone the ticket office from the back room, but is buying tickets for people sitting in the front rooms. The receptionist says which room the ticket is for, so the seat is in the right place.

sections.title: The Option Format
sections.content:
The option carries a single IPv4 address that is the address of a subnet. To get that value, take any IPv4 address on the subnet and AND it with the subnet mask: the network and subnet bits are left alone and the remaining address bits are set to zero.

On the wire it is three parts: the code 118, a length of 4, and the four bytes of the address. IANA assigned the value 118 for this option code.

When the server is configured to respond to the option, is allocating an address, and the option is present, it MUST allocate the address on the subnet named in the option, or on a subnet on the same network segment as that subnet.
sections.eli5: The option is a tiny label with a number saying what kind of label it is, how long it is, and the name of the subnet you want.

sections.title: Server and Client Behavior
sections.content:
Servers set up to support the option MUST return an identical copy of it to any client that sends it, whether or not the client listed it in a parameter request list. Clients that use the option MUST discard any DHCPOFFER or DHCPACK that does not contain it.

That rule handles servers that do not play along. A server that does not understand the option allocates with its normal algorithms and does not return the option, so the client throws the reply away. A server that understands the option but is administratively set to ignore it MUST ignore it, allocate normally, and MUST NOT return it, with the same result for the client. A server that does honor it MUST NOT offer an address outside the requested subnet or network segment.

The option changes nothing else about the server. For example, handling of a DHCPDISCOVER for an unknown subnet continues to work as before.

Replies need a route back. During a renewal the server may send a DHCPACK directly to the allocated address, but packets from the server might not be routable there. So in every packet the client sends that contains the option, the giaddr field in the BOOTP header MUST be set to an IPv4 address on which the client will accept DHCP packets, for example the address on the subnet connected to the internal network. The address the server replies to MUST be the same one it would choose without the option.
sections.eli5: If the helper does not understand your request for a section, it just gives you a seat anywhere, and you hand the ticket back because it is not what you asked for. You also have to leave a note saying where to send answers, since the answers cannot reach your seat.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC points out that DHCP provides no authentication or security mechanisms, and refers to section 7 of RFC 2131 for the exposures.

The option adds its own risk. Because a client can pick the subnet, it can run a more complete address-pool exhaustion attack: it is no longer limited to the pools on its local subnet.

Therefore servers that implement the option MUST disable it by default, so it has to be switched on through configuration. A server SHOULD also let administrators enable it only under restricted conditions, such as only for explicitly configured client-ids, only for clients on a particular subnet, or only for requests naming certain subnets.
sections.eli5: If anyone could ask for any section, a mischievous person could use up all the seats everywhere. So the hall keeps the option turned off unless the manager turns it on for particular people.

fields.desc: Length of the data that follows, in bytes.

fields.desc: Subnet address: any address on the subnet ANDed with the subnet mask.

messages.label: DHCPDISCOVER + option 118
messages.note: Sent from the internal subnet, naming the subnet where the address is wanted. giaddr is set to an address where the client accepts DHCP packets.

messages.label: DHCPOFFER + identical option 118
messages.note: The offered address is on the requested subnet or its network segment.
